overview.h1: HTS Chapter 62: Woven Apparel — Suits, Jeans, Trousers, Shirts, Dresses, Coats & Bras Tariff Rates (2026)

seo.title: HTS Chapter 62 Tariff Rates 2026: Woven Apparel, Jeans, Shirts, Dresses & Jackets Import Duty | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Searchable duty table for all 1,247 HTS Chapter 62 lines — woven coats, suits, jeans, trousers, shirts, blouses, dresses, sleepwear, swimwear, bras, scarves, ties and gloves — with General, FTA and Column 2 rates and the 2026 extra duty for Vietnam, Bangladesh, China, India and others.

overview.intro:
Chapter 62 covers clothing that is **woven, not knitted**: men's and women's coats and anoraks (6201–6202), **suits, ensembles, blazers, trousers, jeans, shorts, dresses and skirts** (6203–6204), **shirts and blouses** (6205–6206), underwear, sleepwear and robes (6207–6208), babies' garments (6209), coated and nonwoven garments such as disposable hospital gowns and rainwear (6210), swimwear, ski-suits and coveralls (6211), **bras** and corsetry (6212) and accessories — handkerchiefs, scarves, ties, gloves (6213–6217). Knitted garments are chapter 61. Its **1,247 lines** carry base rates from Free to **28.6%** (synthetic women's trousers and ski pants), plus compound rates on wool-blend lines; cotton jeans are 16.6%, men's cotton shirts 19.7%.

Suit and ensemble lines (6203.22–.29, 6204.21–.29) have no rate of their own: each garment pays **the rate it would pay if entered separately**, so the importer gives each garment's line and value. On top of the base rate, since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%** — Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Cambodia, Pakistan and Sri Lanka 10%, Vietnam 12.5%. **China pays 12.5% plus 7.5%** (List 4A) on most lines. Central American apparel entered duty-free under **CAFTA-DR** and Jordanian apparel pay no Section 301 duty, and USMCA goods from Mexico pay none; Canada pays **50%** under Section 338 on 17 subheadings even with USMCA. The U.S. imported **$35.11B** of Chapter 62 goods in 2025: Vietnam $7.18B (20%), Bangladesh $5.23B (15%), China $5.14B (15%) and India $2.69B.

productGroups.label: Men's and boys' overcoats, anoraks, ski jackets, windbreakers and padded vests
productGroups.blurb: Men's overcoats, raincoats, anoraks, ski jackets, windbreakers and padded vests. Cotton 4.4%–9.4%; man-made-fibre anoraks 27.7% unless water resistant (7.1%) or down-filled (4.4%); wool coats 41¢/kg + 16.3%. Recreational performance outerwear (U.S. note 3) has its own lines.

productGroups.label: Women's and girls' overcoats, anoraks, ski jackets, windbreakers and padded vests
productGroups.blurb: The same garments for women and girls: man-made-fibre anoraks and coats 27.7%, water-resistant 7.1%, down-filled 4.4%; cotton 4.4%–8.9%; wool anoraks 14% or 36¢/kg + 16.3%.

productGroups.label: Men's and boys' suits, ensembles, blazers, trousers, jeans and shorts
productGroups.blurb: The chapter's largest heading: men's suits, ensembles, blazers, trousers, **jeans** and shorts. Cotton trousers and jeans 16.6%, synthetic trousers 27.9% (7.1% if water resistant), wool suits 17.5%, synthetic blazers 27.3%. Ensembles pay each garment's own rate.
productGroups.rateSummary: 7.5% · 17.5% · 27.3% · 13.2% · 52.9¢/kg + 21% · 14.9% · 3.8% · 7.1% · The rate applicable to each garment in the ensemble if separately entered · The rate applicable to each garment in the in the ensemble if separately entered · 2.8% · 9.4% · 22% · 1% · 6.5% · 7.6% · 41.9¢/kg + 16.3% · 8.5% · Free · 10.3% · 16.6% · 49.6¢/kg + 19.7% · 27.9% · 12.2%

productGroups.label: Women's and girls' suits, ensembles, blazers, dresses, skirts, trousers and jeans
productGroups.blurb: Women's suits, ensembles, blazers, **dresses**, skirts, trousers, jeans and shorts: cotton jeans and trousers 16.6%, synthetic trousers 28.6%, cotton dresses 8.4%–11.8%, synthetic dresses 16%, wool suits 14%. Ensembles pay each garment's own rate.

productGroups.label: Men's and boys' shirts
productGroups.blurb: Men's and boys' woven shirts: cotton 19.7% (8.7% for certified hand-loomed), man-made fibres 29.1¢/kg + 25.9%, silk 1.1%–7.1%. Knitted polo and T-shirts are chapter 61.

productGroups.label: Women's and girls' blouses and shirts
productGroups.blurb: Women's blouses and shirts: cotton 15.4%, man-made fibres 26.9%, silk 6.9%, wool 17%, other (linen) 6.7%.

productGroups.label: Men's and boys' underpants, pajamas, nightshirts and bathrobes
productGroups.blurb: Men's underpants, nightshirts, pajamas and bathrobes: cotton pajamas 8.9%, man-made-fibre pajamas 16%, man-made-fibre bathrobes 14.9%.

productGroups.label: Women's and girls' slips, panties, nightdresses, pajamas and robes
productGroups.blurb: Women's slips, panties, nightdresses, pajamas and robes: cotton nightdresses and pajamas 8.9%, man-made fibres 16%, silk 1.1%–7.1%. Children's sleepwear must meet the CPSC flammability standards.

productGroups.label: Babies' garments and clothing accessories
productGroups.blurb: Garments and accessories for babies up to 86 cm tall (chapter note 5): cotton 9.3%–14.9%, synthetic up to 28.6%. Heading 6209 wins over every other heading of the chapter.

productGroups.label: Garments of felt, nonwovens or coated and rubberised fabric (disposable gowns, rainwear)
productGroups.blurb: Garments of felt or nonwovens (5602–5603) or of coated, rubberised or laminated fabrics (5903, 5906, 5907): nonwoven disposable hospital gowns Free, rainwear with a fully coated surface 3.3%–3.8%, other 6.2%–16%.

productGroups.label: Track suits, ski-suits, swimwear, coveralls and other garments
productGroups.blurb: Track suits, ski-suits, swimwear, coveralls and other garments: man-made-fibre men's swim trunks 27.8%, women's swimwear 11.8%, ski-suit parts up to 28.6%, coveralls 8.1%–16%.

productGroups.label: Bras, girdles, corsets, braces and suspenders (woven or knitted)
productGroups.blurb: Bras, girdles, corsets, braces and suspenders, knitted or not: bras 16.9% (2.7%–4.8% for some cotton lines), girdles 20%, corsets 23.5%. Sri Lanka is a leading source.

productGroups.label: Handkerchiefs
productGroups.blurb: Handkerchiefs and scarf-type squares with no side over 60 cm (chapter note 8): cotton 7.1%–13.2%, man-made fibres 10.8%, silk 1.1%–3.8%.

productGroups.label: Shawls, scarves, mufflers, mantillas and veils
productGroups.blurb: Shawls, scarves, mufflers, mantillas and veils: silk 1.2%–3.9%, wool 6.7%, synthetic or artificial fibres 5.3%, other 11.3%.

productGroups.label: Ties, bow ties and cravats
productGroups.blurb: Ties, bow ties and cravats: silk 7.2%, man-made fibres 24.8¢/kg + 12.7%, other 5%.

productGroups.label: Gloves, mittens and mitts (not knitted)
productGroups.blurb: Woven gloves, mittens and mitts — work, sports, ski and dress gloves: Free to 23.5%; coated or impregnated work gloves 12.5%–23.5%, hockey gloves Free. Knitted gloves are 6116; leather gloves 4203.

productGroups.label: Other clothing accessories and parts of garments
productGroups.blurb: Other made-up clothing accessories (headbands, sweatbands, pads) and parts of garments: 14.6%, or 2.3% if 70% silk or more.

rateTable.note: Rates shown in grey are inherited from the parent heading. HTSUS states a duty once on the 8-digit line and leaves the 10-digit statistical lines blank; this table resolves each line to the rate that actually applies to it.

workedExamples.title: Men's blue denim jeans from Bangladesh
workedExamples.body: Men's cotton jeans are 16.6% at the general rate, and Bangladesh pays 10% Section 301 (9903.05.26) on top: 26.6%, **$2,660** on a $10,000 shipment. Bangladesh's exception list names no Chapter 62 code, and GSP has been expired since December 31, 2020.

workedExamples.title: Women's polyester trousers from Vietnam
workedExamples.body: Synthetic women's trousers carry the chapter's top ad valorem rate, 28.6%. Vietnam adds 12.5% (9903.05.84): 41.1%, **$4,110** on $10,000. The same trousers made water resistant under additional U.S. note 2 enter under 6204.63.75 at 7.1% — 19.6% with the Section 301 duty.

workedExamples.title: Men's cotton shirts from China
workedExamples.body: Woven cotton shirts are 19.7%. China pays 7.5% under List 4A (9903.88.15) and 12.5% under the 2026 action (9903.05.31): 39.7% in all, **$3,970** on $10,000. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026.

workedExamples.title: A men's polyester jacket-and-trousers ensemble from Vietnam
workedExamples.body: 6203.23.00 has no rate of its own: each garment pays the rate it would pay if entered separately. On a $10,000 ensemble, the importer reports the jacket ($6,000, 6203.33.20, 27.3% = $1,638) and the trousers ($4,000, 6203.43.90, 27.9% = $1,116), and the values must add up to the shipment value. Base duty $2,754, plus 12.5% Section 301 on the whole $10,000 ($1,250): **$4,004**. The tariff calculator asks for those lines and values.

workedExamples.title: Men's cotton shirts from Honduras, with a CAFTA-DR claim
workedExamples.body: Shirts that originate under CAFTA-DR (General Note 29: yarn and fabric from the region, cut and sewn there) and are entered with the SPI "P" are Free, and U.S. note 52(i) (9903.05.95) removes Honduras's 10% Section 301 duty: **$0**. Without a valid claim they pay 29.7% ($2,970).

workedExamples.title: Men's wool blazers from Canada, with a USMCA claim
workedExamples.body: Wool blazers are 17.5%, Free under USMCA, and USMCA also removes Canada's 10% Section 301 duty (9903.05.93). But 6203.31.90 is on the Section 338 list (U.S. note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14), whose 50% applies with or without USMCA: **$5,000** on $10,000 ($7,750 without a USMCA claim).

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** Chapter 62 covers made-up articles of any textile fabric other than wadding, but not knitted or crocheted articles (except bras and corsetry of heading 6212, which may be knitted).

**Note 2.** It does not cover worn clothing of heading 6309 or orthopedic and surgical belts and trusses (9021).

**Note 3.** A **suit** is a set of a suit coat or jacket (outer shell of four or more panels, possibly with a tailored waistcoat) and one lower garment, all in identical fabric of the same construction, color and composition; morning dress, evening dress (tailcoat) and dinner jacket suits are suits too. An **ensemble** is a set of several pieces in identical fabric, put up for retail sale: one upper garment (a waistcoat may be a second) and one or two different lower garments — trousers, overalls, breeches, shorts, a skirt or divided skirt. Track suits and ski-suits are not ensembles.

**Note 4.** Shirts and blouses (6205, 6206) exclude garments with pockets below the waist or a ribbed or tightening waistband; men's shirts cannot be sleeveless.

**Notes 5–6.** Babies' garments are for a body height of 86 cm or less; heading 6209 takes priority over other headings, and 6210 over all others except 6209.

**Note 7.** Ski-suits (6211) are ski overalls or ski ensembles identifiable as worn principally for skiing.

**Note 8.** Scarf-type squares with no side over 60 cm are handkerchiefs (6213); larger ones are 6214.

**Note 9.** Left-over-right closure means men's or boys'; right-over-left women's or girls'. Garments that cannot be identified are classified as women's or girls'.
notes.additionalUsNotes:
**Note 1.** For 6209, "sets" are two or more different garments of 6111, 6209 or 6505 imported together, of corresponding sizes, to be worn together by the same person.

**Note 2. Water resistant.** The water-resistant lines (for example 6201.40.45, 6203.43.11, 6204.63.09, 6211.20.15) need a rubber or plastics application such that not more than 1.0 g of water penetrates after two minutes under a 600 mm head of water (AATCC Test Method 35).

**Note 3. Recreational performance outerwear.** Trousers, overalls, jackets, windbreakers and padded vests of cotton, wool, hemp, bamboo, silk or man-made fibres that are water resistant or treated with plastics, have critically sealed seams and at least five listed features (insulation, zippered pockets, tightening hems, venting, articulated elbows or knees, reinforcement, weatherproof closure, adjustable hood or collar, powder skirt, arm gusset, odor control). Occupational outerwear is excluded, and the importer must keep records proving the features.

**Statistical notes.** Garments of an ensemble are reported separately under the ensemble's 8-digit subheading (note 1); prefixes "H" and "S" identify garments entered under a special access or outward processing program (notes 2–3). The three-digit numbers in brackets (347 cotton trousers, 648 synthetic women's trousers) are textile categories.

tariffUpdates.h1: HTS Chapter 62 Tariff Updates: Woven Apparel, Jeans, Shirts & Dresses (2025–2026)

seo.title: Apparel Tariff Updates 2026: Section 301 on 60 Economies, China List 4A, CAFTA-DR, Canada 338 (HTS Chapter 62) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What changed for U.S. imports of woven apparel since January 2025: unchanged base rates, the end of the IEEPA tariffs and the Section 122 surcharge, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on Vietnam, Bangladesh, India and 57 other economies, China List 4A, CAFTA-DR and Jordan exemptions, and Canada's Section 338 duty.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). All 1,247 Chapter 62 lines carry the same base rates in both.

What changed came on top of the base rate. The 2025 IEEPA duties — 20% on Vietnamese and Bangladeshi apparel, up to 50% on Indian — **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026**, goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%**. For Chapter 62 there is no general exemption; CAFTA-DR apparel entered duty-free (note 52(i)) and Jordanian apparel (note 52(j)) are exempt, and USMCA goods are exempt. China keeps List 4A (7.5%) on 358 of 395 subheadings. Since **August 22, 2026 Canada pays 50%** under Section 338 on 17 subheadings, USMCA or not.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 62 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies with their CAFTA-DR, USMCA and Jordan exemptions, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, China Section 301 List 4A and its exclusion for disposable hospital apparel, the Canada Section 338 duty, Russia's rates in place of column 2, the Nicaragua Section 301 phase-in, the open Section 301 excess-capacity investigations, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended. No antidumping or countervailing duty order and no Section 232 action covers a Chapter 62 line. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.exemption: Vietnam has no exception list for Chapter 62. The 2025 IEEPA reciprocal rate (+20%, 9903.02.69) ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Vietnamese jackets, trousers and dresses pay the base rate plus 12.5%: 29.1% on cotton jeans, 41.1% on synthetic women's trousers.

inEffect.exemption: Bangladesh's exception list (note 52(j)(9), 9903.06.12) names no Chapter 62 subheading. GSP (SPI A, A*), still printed on a few lines, has been expired since December 31, 2020. The 2025 IEEPA rate (+20%, 9903.02.05) ended February 24, 2026; the Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Bangladeshi trousers, jeans and shirts pay the base rate plus 10%: 26.6% on cotton jeans.

inEffect.exemption: List 4A (+7.5%, 9903.88.15, since February 14, 2020) covers 358 of the chapter's 395 eight-digit subheadings; 37 subheadings (102 lines) are not on List 4A — they were on List 4B, which never took effect — among them men's synthetic and 'other' ensembles (6203.23.00, 6204.29.40), rubberised and plastic-coated rainwear (6210.20.30, 6210.30.30, 6210.40.35, 6210.50.35), nonwoven disposable hospital apparel (6210.10.50), synthetic scarves (6214.30), man-made-fibre ties (6215.20), cotton and man-made-fibre handkerchiefs, some gloves and headbands (6217.10.85). The 2026 action adds +12.5% (9903.05.31) on every line. One List 4A exclusion (9903.88.69, note 20(vvv)(iv)) names whole lines — nonwoven disposable surgical and isolation gowns and other hospital apparel (6210.10.50.10, .90) — and runs through November 9, 2026. Note 20(dd)–(ff) keeps List 4A off ensemble entries whose rate comes from a List 1–3 subheading. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Most Chinese woven apparel pays 20% on top of the base rate — 39.7% on cotton shirts, 36.6% on cotton jeans; synthetic ensembles, rainwear, scarves, ties and disposable gowns pay 12.5%.

inEffect.exemption: India has no exception list. GSP (SPI A, A*), still printed on a few lines, has been expired since December 31, 2020. The 2025 IEEPA duties (25% reciprocal plus 25% over Russian oil purchases) ended in February 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Indian dresses, blouses and shirts pay the base rate plus 10%: 18.4% on cotton dresses, 25.4% on cotton blouses.

inEffect.exemption: Indonesia's exception list (note 52(j)(11), 9903.06.16) names no Chapter 62 subheading. GSP (SPI A, A*), still printed on a few lines, has been expired since December 31, 2020. The 2025 IEEPA rate (+19%) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Indonesian apparel pays the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.94), including goods entered under the USMCA tariff preference levels (Chapter 98 subchapter XXIII). Under USMCA a Chapter 62 garment qualifies only if it is cut and sewn in North America from regional yarn and fabric (General Note 11). The 2025 IEEPA duty on Mexico (+25%) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Mexican jeans and trousers pay nothing with a valid USMCA claim; without one, the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: EU goods pay 10% in total in place of the base rate (note 52(k)), so lines with a base rate of 10% or more (wool suits 17.5%, cotton jeans 16.6%, synthetic trousers 28.6%) pay only the base rate. The EU exception list (note 52(j)(2)) names no Chapter 62 subheading. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Italian and other EU suits, trousers and dresses pay 10% in total, or the base rate where it is higher.

inEffect.exemption: Cambodia's exception list (note 52(j)(5), 9903.06.02) names no Chapter 62 subheading. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Cambodian apparel pays the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: Pakistan has no exception list. GSP (SPI A, A*), still printed on a few lines, has been expired since December 31, 2020. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Pakistani trousers and shirts pay the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR (SPI P) are exempt (note 52(i), 9903.05.95). The 26 lines whose General rate is already Free (silk-rich garments, down-filled trousers, disposable hospital apparel, hockey gloves) print no P, so they pay 10%. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Honduran shirts, trousers and other apparel that qualify under CAFTA-DR enter with no duty at all; non-qualifying goods pay the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: CAFTA-DR apparel entered duty-free is exempt (note 52(i), 9903.05.95); the 26 lines Free at the general rate pay 12.5%. Nicaraguan goods that do not originate under CAFTA-DR will also pay the Nicaragua Section 301 duty (9903.89.01): 0% in 2026, 10% from January 1, 2027, 15% from January 1, 2028. The 18% IEEPA rate ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Nicaraguan trousers and shirts that qualify under CAFTA-DR enter duty-free; other goods pay the base rate plus 12.5%.

inEffect.exemption: Guatemala's CAFTA-DR list (note 52(j)(6)(iii), 9903.06.06) covers all 395 Chapter 62 subheadings when CAFTA-DR is claimed, and note 52(i) (9903.05.95) exempts apparel entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR. The 26 lines Free at the general rate print no P and pay 10%. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Guatemalan apparel that qualifies under CAFTA-DR enters with no duty; other goods pay the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: El Salvador's CAFTA-DR list (note 52(j)(7)(iii), 9903.06.09) covers all 395 Chapter 62 subheadings when CAFTA-DR is claimed, and note 52(i) exempts apparel entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR. The 26 lines Free at the general rate print no P and pay 10%. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Salvadoran apparel that qualifies under CAFTA-DR enters with no duty; other goods pay the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.93), but the 50% Section 338 duty (U.S. note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14) on 17 subheadings (74 lines): down-filled and padded sleeveless man-made-fibre anoraks and coats (6201.40.55, .60, 6202.40.10, .55, .60), wool suits, blazers and other trousers (6203.11.90, 6203.31.50, .90, 6203.41.60), synthetic dresses and silk dresses (6204.43.40, 6204.49.10), coated or rubberised man-made-fibre garments (6210.20.50, 6210.40.55, 6210.50.55) and coveralls and jumpsuits (6211.32.90, 6211.33.90, 6211.43.10) applies with or without a USMCA claim. No Chapter 62 line is on the September 29, 2026 import-ban annexes. The IEEPA duty on Canada ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Canadian apparel pays nothing extra with USMCA except the 17 Section 338 subheadings, which pay 50% (60% without a USMCA claim).

inEffect.exemption: Brazil's 25% (9903.05.01, from July 22, 2026) reaches every Chapter 62 line — Brazil's exemption list (note 50(a)(ii)) names none — and the 2026 action adds 12.5% (9903.05.27). The 2025 IEEPA duties (10% reciprocal and 40%) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian apparel pays 37.5% on top of the base rate.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 (2026, 60 economies) + Russia (rates in lieu of column 2)
inEffect.exemption: Russian goods on two glove lines (6216.00.13, 6216.00.38) pay 35% in place of the column 2 rate (9903.90.08, U.S. note 30); all Russian goods pay the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Russian apparel pays the column 2 rate (or 35%) plus 12.5%; trade is negligible.

inEffect.country: Other Section 301 economies (43: Algeria, Angola, Argentina, Australia, Bahamas, Bahrain, Chile, Colombia, …)
inEffect.now: +10% or 10% (in place of base) or +12.5% or 12.5% (in place of base)
inEffect.exemption: Jordan's exception list (note 52(j)(13), 9903.06.20) covers all 395 Chapter 62 subheadings. CAFTA-DR textile goods of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR are exempt (note 52(i), 9903.05.95). Goods properly entered under Chapter 98 — Haiti HOPE/HELP (9820.62.xx), AGOA (9819.11.xx), USMCA tariff preference levels — are outside the duty, except 9802 entries (note 52(a)). No other country list names a Chapter 62 code. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Most other suppliers pay the base rate plus 10% or 12.5%; Jordanian apparel and CAFTA-DR-claimed Central American apparel pay none, and Haiti and AGOA countries such as Kenya are not among the 60 economies.

changes.title: No Chapter 62 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 1,247 Chapter 62 lines carry the same General, FTA and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; no line was added, split or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 4A continues
changes.detail: USTR received requests to continue the 2018–2019 China Section 301 actions, so they stay in effect during the four-year review. For Chapter 62 this keeps +7.5% (9903.88.15) on 358 of 395 subheadings, including cotton trousers, jeans, shirts and dresses.

changes.title: Canadian import bans do not reach Chapter 62
changes.detail: Proclamations 11061–11063 banned some Canadian alcoholic beverages, dairy-scope products and motorcycles over 800 cc from September 29, 2026. No Chapter 62 line is on their annexes.

changes.title: Section 338 list revised; 17 Chapter 62 subheadings listed
changes.detail: Proclamations 11064 and 11065 changed the products on the 9903.03.14 list from September 15, 2026. Revision 21 lists 17 subheadings (74 lines): down-filled and padded sleeveless man-made-fibre anoraks and coats (6201.40.55, .60, 6202.40.10, .55, .60), wool suits, blazers and other trousers (6203.11.90, 6203.31.50, .90, 6203.41.60), synthetic dresses and silk dresses (6204.43.40, 6204.49.10), coated or rubberised man-made-fibre garments (6210.20.50, 6210.40.55, 6210.50.55) and coveralls and jumpsuits (6211.32.90, 6211.33.90, 6211.43.10) in U.S. note 51(b)(3).

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duty of 50% on Chapter 62 apparel
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 put a 50% duty (9903.03.14) on Canadian goods in U.S. note 51(b)(3), which names down and padded synthetic coats, wool suits and blazers, synthetic dresses, coated garments and coveralls (17 subheadings). It is charged even when USMCA is claimed and on top of the 10% Section 301 duty on non-USMCA goods. Planned for August 19, it took effect August 22 after a 3-day suspension (Proclamation 11056).

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies reach every Chapter 62 line
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84) — 10% for Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Cambodia, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Honduras, Guatemala, El Salvador, Mexico and Canada, 12.5% for China, Vietnam, Nicaragua, Egypt and Türkiye, 10% in total for the EU. No Chapter 62 code is on the general exemption list. Exempt: CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods entered duty-free (note 52(i)), Jordan's list (all Chapter 62), Guatemala's and El Salvador's CAFTA-DR lists, USMCA goods (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94) and Chapter 98 entries such as Haiti HOPE/HELP and AGOA apparel. Other FTA claims remove the base rate but not this duty.

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on all goods of Brazil (9903.05.01); no Chapter 62 code is on Brazil's exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii)). From July 24 the 12.5% 2026 action (9903.05.27) is added on top.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) and the tariff preference levels still apply.

changes.title: De minimis exemption suspended indefinitely
changes.detail: CBP's interim final rules keep duty-free de minimis treatment ($800) suspended for shipments by all modes, including mail, so low-value apparel orders pay duty and the extra duties like any other entry. On October 8, 2026 CBP proposed a new low-value shipment entry process.

changes.title: CBP forced-labor guidance: apparel and cotton are high-priority sectors
changes.detail: CBP's operational guidance lists the supply-chain tracing documents it expects for the UFLPA high-priority sectors, which include apparel and cotton products. Garments made wholly or in part in Xinjiang or by a listed entity — including with Xinjiang cotton spun or woven elsewhere — are presumed barred unless the importer rebuts the presumption.

changes.title: AGOA and Haiti HOPE/HELP written into the schedule through 2026
changes.detail: Proclamation 11030 put the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 extensions into the HTS: AGOA duty-free treatment, the regional apparel and third-country fabric programs (9819.11.xx), and Haiti's HOPE/HELP apparel preferences (9820.62.xx, Chapter 98 subchapter XX note 6) all run through December 31, 2026. It also re-designated Gabon.

changes.title: Section 301 investigations of structural excess capacity
changes.detail: USTR opened Section 301 investigations of 16 economies — among them China, Vietnam, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, India and Mexico, the main apparel suppliers — over excess manufacturing capacity. No action has been announced.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. No Chapter 62 subheading was on the product exemption list (9903.03.03). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico (9903.03.07, 9903.03.08) and CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods entered duty-free (9903.03.09) were exempt.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil, India and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) from February 7, 2026. India's 25% reciprocal rate ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24.

changes.title: AGOA and Haiti HOPE/HELP reauthorized through December 31, 2026
changes.detail: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (P.L. 119-75) renewed AGOA retroactively from September 30, 2025, with the third-country fabric program that lets apparel from lesser-developed AGOA countries such as Kenya use fabric from anywhere, and extended Haiti's HOPE/HELP apparel preferences to the same date. GSP remains expired since December 31, 2020.

changes.title: Nicaragua Section 301 tariff phases in from 2027
changes.detail: USTR's action on Nicaragua adds a duty on Nicaraguan goods that do not originate under CAFTA-DR (9903.89.01): 0% in 2026, 10% from January 1, 2027 and 15% from January 1, 2028. It reaches every Chapter 62 line; CAFTA-DR-originating apparel is not covered.

changes.title: China List 4A exclusions extended to November 9, 2026
changes.detail: USTR extended 178 China Section 301 product exclusions, including the one for nonwoven disposable surgical and isolation gowns and other hospital apparel of 6210.10.50. It removes the 7.5% List 4A duty (9903.88.69) but not the 12.5% 2026 duty.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. It applied to every Chapter 62 line on top of List 4A until it ended on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: De minimis duty-free treatment suspended for all countries
changes.detail: Executive Order 14324 suspended duty-free entry of shipments valued at $800 or less from all countries, so direct-to-consumer apparel parcels became dutiable.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84) over India's purchases of Russian oil, on top of the 25% reciprocal rate in force since August 7, 2025: 50% in all on Indian garments. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Country-specific reciprocal rates
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 replaced the 10% baseline with country rates: Vietnam, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka +20%, Cambodia, Indonesia, Pakistan and Thailand +19%, Nicaragua +18%, Jordan and Türkiye +15%, India +25%, and 15% in total for EU goods. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: 40% IEEPA duty on products of Brazil
changes.detail: Executive Order 14323 added 40% on goods of Brazil, on top of the 10% reciprocal duty. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty cut from 125% to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14298 cut the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 10% for 90 days (later extended). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty raised to 125%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14266 raised the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 125%, on top of List 4A and the fentanyl duty.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. No Chapter 62 subheading was on the exemption list. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of List 4A.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01); USMCA-qualifying goods exempt. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10), later raised to +35%; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt. Ended February 24, 2026.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 62 goods were **$35.11B in 2025**, 3.4% less than the $36.33B of 2024 and well below the $44.57B peak of 2022. **Vietnam** shipped **$7.18B** (20%, up 5.4%) and **Bangladesh** **$5.23B** (15%, up 9.6%), mostly trousers, jeans and jackets. **China** fell 34% to **$5.14B** (15%) — it was the top supplier in 2020 at $10.19B. India ($2.69B), Indonesia ($2.24B) and Mexico ($1.77B) follow; Italy ($1.49B) ships mostly tailored and luxury garments, Sri Lanka ($724M) mostly bras.

By product, trousers, jeans and shorts dominate: men's cotton trousers 6203.42 ($4.42B), women's cotton trousers 6204.62 ($4.06B) and men's synthetic trousers 6203.43 ($2.20B), then bras 6212.10 ($1.88B) and men's cotton shirts 6205.20 ($1.68B). Headings 6203 and 6204 together were $18.40B — more than half the chapter.

Imports kept shifting away from China in 2025, when Chinese garments carried List 4A, the IEEPA fentanyl duty and, from April, the reciprocal tariff; Cambodia rose 16% to $1.40B and Bangladesh 10%. Central American suppliers using CAFTA-DR (Honduras $408M, Nicaragua $285M, Guatemala $133M, El Salvador $90M), Jordan ($528M, up 15%), Kenya ($311M) and Haiti ($135M) ship largely duty-free under trade preferences. The IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026; since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5% applies to most Asian suppliers instead. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

industryAreas.intro:
The total rate on a pair of trousers or a shirt depends as much on **where it was sewn** as on the line. Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference — computed from the current tariff schedule with the same engine as the tariff calculator.

Since the IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026, the extra duty is mainly the **Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** (from July 24, 2026): **Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Cambodia, Pakistan and Sri Lanka +10%**, **Vietnam +12.5%**, EU goods 10% in total. **China pays +20%** on most lines (12.5% plus List 4A). **Jordan** and **CAFTA-DR** suppliers claiming duty-free entry pay nothing, **USMCA goods from Mexico pay nothing**, and Canada pays 50% on 17 Section 338 subheadings even with USMCA.

Ensemble lines show the HTS wording "the rate applicable to each garment in the ensemble if separately entered" plus the extra duty: the base part depends on which garments are in the set and their values, which the tariff calculator asks for.

rule.label: With a CAFTA-DR claim (SPI P), as shown: Free and no Section 301 duty on the 1,221 lines that print P — apparel entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR is exempt (note 52(i), 9903.05.95). The 26 lines already Free at the general rate (silk-rich garments, down-filled trousers, disposable hospital apparel, hockey gloves) print no P and pay 12.5% (9903.05.58). Goods that do not qualify pay the base rate plus 12.5%. Non-originating goods will also pay 10% from 2027 (9903.89.01).

rule.label: With a CAFTA-DR claim (SPI P), as shown: Free and no Section 301 duty on the 1,221 lines that print P — apparel entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR is exempt (note 52(i), 9903.05.95); Guatemala's CAFTA-DR list (9903.06.06) also covers every subheading. The 26 lines already Free at the general rate (silk-rich garments, down-filled trousers, disposable hospital apparel, hockey gloves) print no P and pay 10% (9903.05.40). Goods that do not qualify pay the base rate plus 10%.

assumptions: Each total was computed by the official-measures calculator engine (the same data as the tariff calculator: measures.json, HTSUS 2026 Revision 21) for goods entered on 2026-10-13, priced on a $10,000 shipment and 1,000 units for per-unit rates.
Ranges like "Free · 11.8%" mean the group has lines with different base rates; select a cell to see which lines carry which rate.
A per-unit rate plus a percentage cannot be added into one number without the shipment’s weight, count or volume, so it is shown as written.

Preferences: USMCA (S) is applied for Canada and Mexico on the "USMCA-qualifying" side; JO for Jordan; P for Honduras; P for Nicaragua; P for Guatemala; P for El Salvador. GSP (A, A+) has lapsed and is not applied. Other preferences are not applied.
Any other country shows the range across every country not listed (column 2 countries — Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Belarus — aside), without preferences.
The IEEPA duties (9903.01.xx, 9903.02.xx) are still printed in the schedule but ended February 24, 2026, and the Section 122 surcharge (9903.03.01) expired July 23, 2026; neither is applied.

Ensemble lines (6203.22.30–6203.29.30, 6204.21.00–6204.29.40) are shown in the HTS wording: the base rate is each garment's own rate on its own value, so it cannot be priced without the garments; the extra duty is added on the whole value.
EU rates of "10% in total" replace the base rate when it is lower (U.S. note 52(k)); where the base rate is higher, only the base rate applies.

Honduras, Nicaragua, Guatemala and El Salvador are priced with a CAFTA-DR claim (SPI P): apparel entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR is exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(i)). Jordan is priced with its FTA claim.

Not in the grid: Haiti HOPE/HELP (9820.62.xx) and AGOA (9819.11.xx) apparel entered under Chapter 98, USMCA tariff preference levels, the 9802.00.80 U.S.-components provision, and the UFLPA presumption and FTC/CPSC rules — see Import documents.
No antidumping or countervailing duty order and no Section 232 action covers a Chapter 62 line.
industryAreas.exemptionCheck: Read U.S. notes 2, 20, 30, 31, 50, 51 and 52 to Chapter 99 subchapter III and subchapter II in the 2026 Revision 21. Note 52(b) (9903.05.86) names no Chapter 62 code. Note 52(i) (9903.05.95) exempts CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods entered duty-free. Note 52(j) lists name Chapter 62 codes only for Jordan (all 395 subheadings, 9903.06.20) and, for CAFTA-DR claims, Guatemala and El Salvador (all 395, 9903.06.06, 9903.06.09); the UK, EU, Swiss, Malaysian, Cambodian, Argentine, Bangladeshi, Taiwanese, Indonesian and Ecuadorian lists name none. Note 52(a) leaves Chapter 98 entries (AGOA, Haiti) outside the duty except 9802. Note 50(a)(ii) names no Chapter 62 code for Brazil. Note 51(b)(3) puts 17 Chapter 62 subheadings on the Canada Section 338 list. Note 20(s) puts 358 of 395 subheadings on China List 4A; the other 37 were on the suspended List 4B; note 20(vvv)(iv) excludes 6210.10.50.10 and .90 through November 9, 2026; note 20(dd)–(ff) limits List 4A on ensemble entries. Note 31 names no Chapter 62 code. Note 30 lists two glove lines for Russia. The Section 122 exemption list (9903.03.03) named no Chapter 62 code. The subchapter II duty suspension for babies' linen apparel (9902.13.67) expired December 31, 2020. No Section 232 heading reaches a Chapter 62 line, and a Federal Register search of Commerce notices found no antidumping or countervailing duty order on Chapter 62 goods.

tariffEngineering.h1: Importing Woven Apparel (HTS Ch. 62): Origin Rules, UFLPA, Labeling, Flammability & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Clothing: Apparel Origin Rules, UFLPA, FTC Labels, CPSC & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Chapter 62) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The CBP, FTC and CPSC rules for each HTS Chapter 62 line — apparel country of origin (19 CFR 102.21), manufacturer ID, UFLPA, fibre-content and care labels, clothing and children's sleepwear flammability — and the legal ways to pay less: USMCA and its preference levels, CAFTA-DR, Jordan, AGOA, Haiti HOPE/HELP, classification, first sale and drawback.

tariffEngineering.intro:
For most Chapter 62 garments **the country of origin is the country where the garment was wholly assembled** — cut panels sewn together — whatever the origin of the fabric (19 CFR 102.21); scarves, shawls and handkerchiefs (6213–6214) take the origin of the fabric instead. Every entry names the manufacturer by manufacturer identification code, garments with cotton face the UFLPA presumption, and garments sold at retail need fibre-content, origin and care labels (16 CFR parts 303 and 423). Clothing textiles must meet the CPSC flammability standard, and children's sleepwear the stricter sleepwear standards.

The ways to pay less are in the schedule: **USMCA** (with tariff preference levels for non-regional fabric), **CAFTA-DR** for Central American apparel (also exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty), **Jordan**, **AGOA** and **Haiti HOPE/HELP** through 2026, line-by-line classification (water-resistant and recreational performance outerwear lines), **first-sale valuation**, **drawback** and **foreign-trade zones**. Each depends on a document, listed below with its regulation.

levers.title: Know where the garment is assembled — that is usually the country of origin
levers.saves: The difference between country rates: 0% for Haiti or Kenya, +10% for Bangladesh or India, +12.5% for Vietnam, +20% for China
levers.appliesTo: Headings 6201–6212 and 6215–6217 (where wholly assembled); 6213–6214 take the origin of the fabric
levers.document: Production records showing where the panels were cut and sewn, and the MID of the assembling factory on the entry.
levers.caveat: Origin moves only with real assembly: pressing, packing, labeling or minor sewing in a third country does not change it, and CBP denies entry to goods from factories it cannot verify (19 CFR 102.24). Moving assembly does not remove the UFLPA presumption for Xinjiang cotton.

levers.title: Claim USMCA — or a USMCA tariff preference level — on garments cut and sewn in Mexico or Canada
levers.saves: The base rate (up to 28.6%) and the 10% Section 301 duty for Mexico or Canada
levers.appliesTo: All lines, for garments cut and sewn in North America from regional yarn and fabric (General Note 11, chapter 62 rules, with the pocket-bag and sewing-thread rules); garments of non-regional fabric within the annual tariff preference levels (9823.52.01, 9823.53.01)
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, with the SPI "S" on the entry line; for a tariff preference level, the TPL heading and its eligibility requirements.
levers.caveat: Asian fabric sewn in Mexico qualifies only within a TPL. For Canada, USMCA does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on down and padded synthetic coats, wool suits and blazers, synthetic dresses, coated garments and coveralls (17 subheadings). The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 98 subch. XXIII, U.S. note 11 (TPLs)

levers.title: Claim CAFTA-DR — it also removes the 2026 Section 301 duty
levers.saves: The base rate and the 10%–12.5% Section 301 duty on Central American and Dominican apparel
levers.appliesTo: Garments of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua that originate under General Note 29 (yarn-forward, with the short-supply list) and are entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR (SPI P)
levers.document: A CAFTA-DR claim with the SPI "P" on the entry line and records supporting origin; for Guatemala and El Salvador the exemption heading 9903.06.06 or 9903.06.09, for the others 9903.05.95.
levers.caveat: Lines already Free at the general rate print no P and keep the Section 301 duty. Non-originating Nicaraguan goods will pay 10% from 2027 and 15% from 2028 (9903.89.01).

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(i), (j)

levers.title: Source from Jordan
levers.saves: The base rate under the Jordan FTA, and the 10% Section 301 duty for every Chapter 62 subheading
levers.appliesTo: Garments that are products of Jordan under the FTA rules (General Note 18), entered with the SPI "JO"; Jordan's exception list (9903.06.20) covers all 395 Chapter 62 subheadings
levers.document: Proof of origin under the U.S.–Jordan FTA and the SPI "JO" on the entry line.
levers.caveat: The exception list removes the Section 301 duty even without an FTA claim, but the base rate stays unless the goods qualify.

levers.title: Use AGOA or Haiti HOPE/HELP for African and Haitian apparel (through December 31, 2026)
levers.saves: The full base rate — up to 28.6% — on garments that would otherwise pay it; neither Haiti nor AGOA countries such as Kenya, Madagascar or Lesotho are among the 60 Section 301 economies
levers.appliesTo: Apparel assembled in AGOA beneficiary countries (9819.11.03–9819.11.30; lesser-developed countries may use third-country fabric under 9819.11.12) and apparel assembled in Haiti under the HOPE/HELP rules (9820.62.05–9820.62.30)
levers.document: The Chapter 98 heading with the Chapter 62 number; for AGOA, a textile certificate of origin and a visa from the beneficiary country.
levers.caveat: Both programs are authorized only through December 31, 2026 (Proclamation 11030). Haiti's preferences have value-content rules or annual quantity limits.

citations.label: HTSUS Chapter 98, subchapters XIX and XX

levers.title: Check the classification line by line — fibre, water resistance and outerwear features move the rate
levers.saves: Up to 21 points of base rate: synthetic trousers are 27.9%–28.6%, but 7.1% if water resistant (additional U.S. note 2); man-made-fibre anoraks 27.7%, but 7.1% if water resistant and 4.4% if down-filled; recreational performance outerwear has its own lines
levers.appliesTo: Coats and anoraks (6201, 6202), trousers (6203.4x, 6204.6x), ski-suits (6211.20) and any blend
levers.document: A binding ruling request to CBP (19 CFR part 177) with fibre content by weight, construction and test results (AATCC 35 for water resistance); for recreational performance outerwear, records proving each feature (additional U.S. note 3(c)).
levers.caveat: Classification follows the garment as imported and its real construction; a coating or feature added only to change the line must still meet the note's test. Rulings bind only the transaction described.

citations.label: HTSUS Chapter 62 notes and additional U.S. notes 2–3

levers.title: Report ensembles garment by garment
levers.saves: Nothing on its own — but it gets the duty right: each garment of a suit-less ensemble pays its own rate on its own value, so the cheaper-rated pieces are not charged the higher rate
levers.document: An invoice that values each garment of the set separately, with the 10-digit line each garment would be entered under (statistical note 1).
levers.caveat: The pieces must be of identical fabric and put up for retail sale (chapter note 3(b)); otherwise each garment is classified on its own. For China, 6203.23.00 and 6204.29.40 are not on List 4A even though their garments are.

citations.label: HTSUS Chapter 62 note 3 and statistical note 1

levers.title: Assemble abroad from U.S.-cut components (9802.00.80)
levers.saves: Duty only on the value added abroad, not on the U.S. fabric and components
levers.appliesTo: Garments assembled abroad from fabricated components cut in the United States and exported ready for assembly
levers.document: A foreign assembler's declaration and the endorsed importer's declaration with costs of the U.S. components.
levers.caveat: The 2026 Section 301 duty still applies to the value of the assembly (note 52(a)); bleaching, garment-dyeing or stone-washing abroad can disqualify the goods.

levers.title: Use the China List 4A exclusion for disposable hospital apparel
levers.saves: The 7.5% List 4A duty (the 12.5% 2026 duty still applies)
levers.appliesTo: Nonwoven disposable surgical and isolation gowns and other hospital apparel of 6210.10.50.10 and .90, entered by November 9, 2026
levers.document: Heading 9903.88.69 reported with the statistical number.
levers.caveat: The exclusion ends after November 9, 2026 unless USTR extends it again.

levers.title: Value at the first sale for export when you buy through a middleman
levers.saves: Every ad valorem duty — base rate and Section 301 — is charged on a lower value when the factory's price to a trading company is lower than the price you pay
levers.appliesTo: All lines bought through a trading company, agent-buyer or vendor rather than straight from the factory
levers.document: Proof that the first sale was a bona fide sale for export to the United States at arm's length: the factory invoice, contracts and payment records.
levers.caveat: Only a sale clearly destined for the U.S. qualifies, and the importer must be able to show the earlier price at entry.

levers.title: Claim drawback when garments are exported or destroyed
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid, including Section 301 duties, on garments re-exported unused or destroyed
levers.appliesTo: All lines — useful for unsold or returned stock shipped to Canadian, Mexican or other markets
levers.document: A drawback claim filed in ACE within 5 years of import, with records linking the import to the export.
levers.caveat: Only duties actually paid are refunded; USMCA limits drawback on goods exported to Canada or Mexico.

levers.title: Hold, relabel or kit garments in a foreign-trade zone
levers.saves: No duty on garments re-exported from the zone, and duty deferred until they enter the U.S. market
levers.appliesTo: Any line — useful for apparel distributed to Canada, Mexico and the U.S. from one stock
levers.document: Zone admission (CBP Form 214) and the zone operator's inventory records.
levers.caveat: Garments entered for U.S. consumption from a zone pay the duties in force on the entry date.

rules.title: Apparel country of origin: for 6201–6212 and 6215–6217 the country where the garment was wholly assembled (one-piece articles: where the fabric was formed); for handkerchiefs, scarves and shawls (6213–6214) the country where the fabric was formed, or for some silk and man-made-fibre ones the country that dyed and printed it (102.21(e)(2))
Manufacturer identification code (MID) of the company that performed the origin-conferring operation on every entry — this replaced the textile declaration, eliminated in 2011
Entry is denied for apparel from a company named in the Federal Register for illegal transshipment or for being unable to verify production
Invoice details for wearing apparel: fibre content by weight, whether woven or knit, the manufacturer and the country where made, among the textile-specific data

UFLPA: goods made wholly or in part in Xinjiang or by an entity on the UFLPA Entity List are presumed made with forced labor and excluded unless the importer rebuts it; apparel and cotton are high-priority sectors, so garments need tracing documents back to the cotton or fibre
Textile Act labels on every garment sold at retail: generic fibre content by percentage, the RN or company name, and the country where made ("Made in Vietnam")

Care Labeling Rule: a permanent label with washing or dry-cleaning instructions on textile wearing apparel; gloves and hats are outside the definition, and fully reversible garments without pockets are exempt
Wool Products Labeling Act: wool and cashmere coats, suits, blazers and scarves must show wool fibre content and origin; fur trim needs a Fur Act label

Flammability of clothing textiles: fabrics used in apparel must not be Class 3 (dangerously flammable). Plain fabrics of 2.6 oz/yd² or more and all-acrylic, modacrylic, nylon, olefin, polyester or wool fabrics need no testing to support a guaranty; gloves up to 14 inches and interlinings are outside the standard
Children's sleepwear sizes 0–14 (nightgowns, pajamas, robes) must meet the stricter sleepwear flammability standards unless tight-fitting or an infant garment of 9 months or smaller

Children's apparel (12 and under) needs a Children's Product Certificate based on third-party testing (lead in paint and accessories, flammability), and upper outerwear in sizes 2T–16 with neck or hood drawstrings is a substantial product hazard
Country-of-origin marking on the garment (in practice, the FTC label) or its retail container

groups.label: Men's and boys' overcoats, anoraks, ski jackets, windbreakers and padded vests
groups.note: Origin is where the coat was assembled. Down-filled, water-resistant and recreational performance outerwear lines carry much lower rates than plain man-made-fibre anoraks (27.7%). Children's jackets with hood drawstrings are a substantial product hazard. Five subheadings are on Canada's Section 338 list.

groups.label: Women's and girls' overcoats, anoraks, ski jackets, windbreakers and padded vests
groups.note: As 6201, for women's and girls' coats. Down-filled and padded man-made-fibre coats (6202.40.10, .55, .60) are on Canada's Section 338 list.

groups.label: Men's and boys' suits, ensembles, blazers, trousers, jeans and shorts
groups.note: Origin is where assembled. Ensembles pay each garment's rate and must be valued garment by garment. Men's cotton jeans are 6203.42.45.11 (6203.42.07.11 if recreational performance outerwear). Wool suits and blazers are on Canada's Section 338 list.

groups.label: Women's and girls' suits, ensembles, blazers, dresses, skirts, trousers and jeans
groups.note: Origin is where assembled. Ensembles pay each garment's rate. Women's jeans are 6204.62.80.11. Synthetic and silk dresses (6204.43.40, 6204.49.10) are on Canada's Section 338 list.

groups.label: Men's and boys' shirts
groups.note: Origin is where assembled. Cotton shirts carry 19.7% and need UFLPA cotton tracing; man-made-fibre shirts carry a compound rate.

groups.label: Women's and girls' blouses and shirts
groups.note: Origin is where assembled. Cotton blouses 15.4%, man-made fibres 26.9%.

groups.label: Men's and boys' underpants, pajamas, nightshirts and bathrobes
groups.note: Children's pajamas and robes must meet the sleepwear flammability standards (16 CFR parts 1615, 1616).

groups.label: Women's and girls' slips, panties, nightdresses, pajamas and robes
groups.note: Children's nightgowns, pajamas and robes must meet the sleepwear flammability standards; adult sleepwear meets 16 CFR part 1610.

groups.label: Babies' garments and clothing accessories
groups.note: Babies' garments (body height up to 86 cm) are children's products needing a Children's Product Certificate; sleepwear for infants of 9 months or smaller is outside the sleepwear standards but must meet part 1610.

groups.label: Garments of felt, nonwovens or coated and rubberised fabric (disposable gowns, rainwear)
groups.note: Nonwoven disposable hospital apparel (6210.10.50) is Free and excluded from China List 4A through November 9, 2026. Coated man-made-fibre garments (6210.20.50, 6210.40.55, 6210.50.55) are on Canada's Section 338 list.

groups.label: Track suits, ski-suits, swimwear, coveralls and other garments
groups.note: Swimwear, ski-suits and coveralls; ski-suits must meet chapter note 7. Coveralls of 6211.32.90, 6211.33.90 and 6211.43.10 are on Canada's Section 338 list.

groups.label: Bras, girdles, corsets, braces and suspenders (woven or knitted)
groups.note: Bras are classified here whether woven or knitted. Origin is where assembled.

groups.label: Handkerchiefs
groups.note: Handkerchiefs take the origin of the fabric. Squares over 60 cm a side are 6214.

groups.label: Shawls, scarves, mufflers, mantillas and veils
groups.note: Scarves and shawls take the origin of the country where the fabric was formed; wool and cashmere need Wool Act labels.

groups.label: Ties, bow ties and cravats
groups.note: Origin is where assembled. Man-made-fibre ties (6215.20) are not on China List 4A.

groups.label: Gloves, mittens and mitts (not knitted)
groups.note: Gloves up to 14 inches are outside the clothing flammability standard. Two lines carry Russia's 35% rate.

groups.label: Other clothing accessories and parts of garments
groups.note: Accessories of two or more parts take the origin of assembly; one-piece accessories and parts take the origin of the fabric.

tariffEngineering.disclaimer: A checklist of where the rules are, with links to the regulations — not legal advice. Exception lists, China exclusions, the Canada Section 338 list and the AGOA and Haiti programs change by proclamation and notice; check them before each shipment.

finalConclusion.h1: HTS Chapter 62 FAQ: HS Codes & Import Tariffs for Jeans, Trousers, Shirts, Dresses, Jackets & Bras

seo.title: Jeans, Shirt, Dress & Jacket HS Code and Apparel Tariff FAQ 2026 (HTS Chapter 62) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about importing woven clothing: the HS code for jeans, pants, shirts, dresses, jackets, suits, bras, scarves and gloves, and the 2026 tariffs on clothing from China, Vietnam, Bangladesh, India and Mexico.
keywords: tariff on clothing from india to usa

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about importing woven clothing into the U.S. — HS codes, tariffs by country and entry rules. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: Chapter 62 base rates run from Free to 28.6% and are unchanged since January 2025: cotton jeans and trousers 16.6%, synthetic trousers 27.9%–28.6%, men's cotton shirts 19.7%, cotton blouses 15.4%, bras 16.9%. Ensembles pay each garment's own rate.

Since July 24, 2026 Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Cambodia, Pakistan and Sri Lanka pay 10% Section 301 on top of the base rate, Vietnam 12.5%, EU suppliers 10% in total. China pays 20% on most lines (12.5% plus List 4A).

CAFTA-DR apparel entered duty-free, Jordanian apparel and USMCA goods pay no Section 301 duty; Haiti and AGOA countries are outside it, with their apparel preferences in force through December 31, 2026.
Canada pays 50% under Section 338 on 17 Chapter 62 subheadings, even with USMCA. The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge July 23, 2026.

Origin is where the garment is sewn, not where the fabric came from (19 CFR 102.21), but cotton garments still face the UFLPA presumption for Xinjiang cotton. No antidumping or countervailing order covers Chapter 62.

faqs.question: What does HTS Chapter 62 cover?
faqs.answer: Woven (not knitted) clothing and accessories: coats and anoraks (6201–6202), suits, ensembles, blazers, trousers, jeans, shorts, dresses and skirts (6203–6204), shirts and blouses (6205–6206), underwear and sleepwear (6207–6208), babies' garments (6209), coated and nonwoven garments (6210), swimwear and ski-suits (6211), bras (6212), handkerchiefs, scarves, ties, gloves and other accessories (6213–6217). Knitted clothing is chapter 61.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and tariff for jeans?
faqs.answer: Men's blue denim jeans of cotton are 6203.42.45.11, women's 6204.62.80.11 (boys' and girls' have their own lines); both carry 16.6%. Denim jeans of synthetic fibres are 6203.43 or 6204.63 at 27.9%–28.6%; knitted jeggings are chapter 61. From Bangladesh jeans pay 26.6% in all, from Vietnam 29.1%, from China 36.6%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for pants and trousers?
faqs.answer: Men's and boys' woven trousers and shorts are 6203.41 (wool), 6203.42 (cotton, 16.6%), 6203.43 (synthetic, 27.9%) and 6203.49 (other); women's and girls' are 6204.61–6204.69 (cotton 16.6%, synthetic 28.6%). Water-resistant synthetic trousers meeting additional U.S. note 2 are 7.1%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for shirts and blouses?
faqs.answer: Men's and boys' woven shirts are 6205: cotton 6205.20 (19.7%), man-made fibres 6205.30 (29.1¢/kg + 25.9%). Women's and girls' blouses and shirts are 6206: cotton 6206.30 (15.4%), man-made fibres 6206.40 (26.9%), silk 6206.10 (6.9%). Knitted shirts, polos and T-shirts are chapter 61.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for dresses?
faqs.answer: Woven women's and girls' dresses are 6204.41–6204.49: cotton 6204.42 (mostly 8.4%), synthetic 6204.43 (16%), artificial fibres such as rayon 6204.44, silk and other 6204.49. Synthetic and silk dresses (6204.43.40, 6204.49.10) from Canada pay a 50% Section 338 duty.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for jackets and coats?
faqs.answer: Woven coats, anoraks, windbreakers and padded vests are 6201 (men's) and 6202 (women's). Man-made-fibre anoraks are 27.7%, 7.1% if water resistant and 4.4% if down-filled (15% or more down and plumage); cotton 4.4%–9.4%. Suit-type jackets and blazers are 6203.3x and 6204.3x; leather jackets are 4203.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for suits, blazers and ensembles, and how are ensembles taxed?
faqs.answer: Suits are 6203.11–.19 and 6204.11–.19 (wool 17.5% men's, 14% women's); blazers 6203.31–.39 and 6204.31–.39. Ensembles (6203.22–.29, 6204.21–.29) pay the rate of each garment as if entered separately: the importer lists each garment's line and value, each is charged its own rate, and extra duties apply to the whole value.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for bras?
faqs.answer: Brassieres are 6212.10 whether woven or knitted, mostly at 16.9%. Girdles are 6212.20 (20%), corsets 6212.30 (23.5%), braces and suspenders 6212.90 (6.6%). Sri Lankan bras pay 26.9% in all with the 10% Section 301 duty.

faqs.question: What are the HS codes for scarves and gloves?
faqs.answer: Woven scarves and shawls are 6214: silk 6214.10 (1.2%–3.9%), wool 6214.20 (6.7%), synthetic 6214.30 and artificial 6214.40 (5.3%). Squares no more than 60 cm a side are handkerchiefs (6213). Woven gloves are 6216 (Free to 23.5%); knitted gloves are 6116 and leather gloves 4203.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on clothing from China in 2026?
searchedAs: tariff on apparel from china to usa
current tariff on clothing from china
are there tariffs on clothing from china
faqs.answer: For Chapter 62, every line pays 12.5% under the 2026 Section 301 action (9903.05.31), and 358 of 395 subheadings also pay 7.5% under List 4A: 20% on top of the base rate — 39.7% on cotton shirts, 36.6% on cotton jeans. Synthetic ensembles, rainwear, synthetic scarves and ties pay 12.5% extra. The IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on clothing from India to the USA?
searchedAs: tariff on clothing from india to usa
us tariff on garments from india
tariffs on clothes from india to us
faqs.answer: Indian woven apparel pays the base rate plus 10% Section 301 (9903.05.44), with no exception list: 18.4% on most cotton dresses, 25.4% on cotton blouses, 26.6% on cotton trousers. India's 50% IEEPA rate of late 2025 ended in February 2026; GSP has been expired since 2020.

faqs.question: What are the tariffs on clothing from Vietnam and Bangladesh?
searchedAs: us apparel imports bangladesh vs india
faqs.answer: Vietnam pays the base rate plus 12.5% (9903.05.84) and Bangladesh plus 10% (9903.05.26) under the 2026 Section 301 action; neither has an exception list for Chapter 62. Cotton jeans pay 29.1% from Vietnam and 26.6% from Bangladesh. Their 20% IEEPA rates ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on clothing from Mexico and Canada?
faqs.answer: Garments that qualify under USMCA — cut and sewn in North America from regional yarn and fabric, or within a tariff preference level — enter Free and pay no Section 301 duty. Other Mexican and Canadian garments pay the base rate plus 10%. Canada also pays 50% under Section 338 on 17 subheadings (wool suits, down coats, synthetic dresses), with or without USMCA.

faqs.question: Is apparel from Central America and Haiti duty-free?
faqs.answer: CAFTA-DR apparel from Honduras, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador, the Dominican Republic and Costa Rica that meets the yarn-forward rule enters Free with the SPI P and is exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(i)). Haitian apparel can enter Free under HOPE/HELP (9820.62.xx) through December 31, 2026, and Haiti is not among the Section 301 economies.

faqs.question: Where does the U.S. import woven apparel from?
faqs.answer: In 2025 the U.S. imported $35.11B of Chapter 62 goods: Vietnam $7.18B (20%), Bangladesh $5.23B (15%), China $5.14B (15%, down 34% on 2024), India $2.69B, Indonesia $2.24B and Mexico $1.77B, then Italy, Cambodia, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Trousers and jeans (6203–6204) are more than half of the total.
